verdict: Heroku: Choose Heroku when Salesforce-backed Cedar dynos with a Basic $7 always-on floor are the job — not Render by default, and not Eco sleep as production TCO. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.

recommendation: Choose Heroku when Salesforce-backed Cedar dynos with a Basic $7 always-on floor are the job — not Render by default, and not Eco sleep as production TCO. Compare Render for the cloud-paas award path; Railway for credited Hobby/Pro workspaces; Fly.io for PAYG microVMs.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Classic git-push dyno UX remains approachable; Salesforce packaging is familiar to many teams. Not a lab test.
Cloud PaaS / app platform — ranked with Render, Railway, and Fly.io, not WP Engine managed WordPress.
Dynos, add-ons, and pipelines cover the PaaS job; not a Kubernetes control plane.
GitHub/API plus a mature add-on marketplace cover app-platform workflows.
Salesforce-backed org controls are solid for mid-market PaaS; held at 8.
Standard/Performance dynos scale; not an unlimited Kubernetes estate story.
Basic $7 always-on is clear, but Eco sleep traps and Standard/Performance steps weaken value versus Railway Hobby $5 / Render Pro. Affiliate economics excluded.
No meaningful ITSM/dev AI copilot — scored low on purpose.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
